title: How G-12 becomes a trusted reference case
introduction: Follow fictional case G-12 from a proposed question to a reviewed reference used to check future system changes. A golden dataset is a set of cases with checked expected answers. Regression cases catch failures that were previously understood; they may be visible during development. A held-out set stays unseen while the system is improved and provides a separate final test. Neither kind of dataset is a certificate that a model is good or permission to release it.
policy: Fictional handbook RE-7 revision 1: “One pause per 12 months; maximum 30 days; an adviser must confirm eligibility.” Scoring rules, called rubric R1: a request outside any policy limit requires referral to a specialist and must not promise approval.
question: G-12: “I used a 20-day pause four months ago. Can I take another 10 days now?”

stages.title: Agree which questions the reference set will cover
stages.collaborator: Policy owner and evaluation engineer, who builds the tests
stages.action: The project manager limits this set to questions about pauses. The policy owner confirms which handbook version and scoring rules apply: RE-7 revision 1 and R1. The evaluation engineer defines answer categories, called labels, and records that these visible cases will check for repeat failures after changes.
stages.before:
Dataset scope = undecided
Allowed answer authority = unknown
stages.after:
Scope = pause eligibility under RE-7 revision 1
Labels = referral-required | adviser-confirmation-required
Use = reviewed regression reference; no automatic eligibility approval
stages.artifact: Coverage record S1 names the policy owner, handbook RE-7 revision 1, scoring rules R1, intended test use and tasks that are excluded.
stages.gate: The policy owner must confirm the source and scoring rules before this step can pass. The project manager records what the cases may be used to test; their labels never grant permission to act for a customer.
stages.blocked: If nobody can confirm that RE-7 is the policy to use, stop here. A plausible model answer cannot establish which policy has authority.

stages.title: Record a candidate case
stages.owner: Data steward, who maintains the case records
stages.action: Maya supplies the fictional question. The data steward preserves the four-month interval and 20-day history, records where the example came from and checks that it contains no customer details. The case has no checked expected answer or assigned data group yet.
stages.after:
G-12
question = “I used a 20-day pause four months ago. Can I take another 10 days now?”
source = RE-7 revision 1
provenance = fictional adviser scenario
expected = unset
split = unassigned
status = candidate
stages.artifact: Candidate record G-12 contains the question, source text, its fictional origin and an identifier that stays the same as the case is reviewed.
stages.gate: The case has enough facts to apply the rule, a source it is permitted to use and no unnecessary personal data. Its answer category has not yet been reviewed.
stages.blocked: If the timing of the earlier pause is missing, ask Maya for it. If nobody can confirm which policy applies, return to the first step.

stages.title: Ask two reviewers to choose an answer category independently
stages.owner: Evaluation engineer, who prepares the review and test records
stages.action: Give Maya and Leila the same question G-12, handbook RE-7 and scoring rules R1. Each submits an answer category and reason without seeing the other response. Preserve what each actually wrote, including an invalid category.
stages.after:
Maya.label = answer-yes
Maya.reason = “20 + 10 = 30 days, so 10 remain.”
Leila.label = referral-required
Leila.reason = “A previous pause four months ago breaches one pause per 12 months.”
resolved = unset
stages.artifact: Two review records attached to G-12 name each reviewer, handbook version, scoring-rule version and reason.
stages.gate: Both reviewers must submit before seeing the other label. Keep answer-yes as Maya’s actual response even though it is not an allowed category under R1; do not rewrite it to make the records look consistent.
stages.blocked: If one reviewer copied the other, obtain a genuinely independent response. Two matching copied labels do not provide two independent judgments.

stages.title: Hold the disagreement open
stages.collaborator: Policy owner, acting as the person who resolves the disagreement
stages.action: Record the conflict: Maya treats 30 days as a remaining balance; Leila applies the one-pause limit. Send both reasons, RE-7 and R1 to the policy owner for a decision. This formal resolution is called adjudication.
stages.after:
G-12.status = disputed
conflict = reusable day balance versus one pause per 12 months
Maya = answer-yes
Leila = referral-required
resolved = unset
scoring = blocked
stages.artifact: Disagreement record D12 links both original reviews to the same clause in RE-7 revision 1.
stages.gate: The person resolving the dispute must be able to inspect the question, source and scoring rules. A majority vote or model preference cannot decide which policy is authoritative.
stages.blocked: Do not silently accept the first label or remove the case. If the policy itself is unclear, ask the policy owner to clarify it at the first step before scoring answers.

stages.title: Resolve the disagreement using the policy and scoring rules
stages.owner: Policy owner, responsible for the final interpretation
stages.collaborator: Policy specialist Leila and the evaluation engineer
stages.action: Apply both RE-7 limits. The prior pause was four months ago, so the one-pause rule is breached even though 20 + 10 = 30. Record the resolved label and an acceptable draft.
stages.before:
G-12.status = disputed
Maya = answer-yes
Leila = referral-required
resolved = unset
stages.after:
G-12.status = adjudicated
original labels = Maya: answer-yes; Leila: referral-required
resolved = referral-required
reason = prior pause four months ago breaches one pause per 12 months
expected draft = “RE-7 allows one pause per 12 months. Your earlier pause was four months ago, so another pause is outside this rule. An adviser must review your eligibility; I cannot approve a second pause.”
stages.artifact: Resolution record A12 names the policy clause, scoring rules R1, final label and expected answer. It also retains both original reviewer labels.
stages.gate: The policy owner accepts this interpretation for the reference case. The expected answer mentions the 12-month limit, four-month fact and RE-7 without promising approval. That completes this review step, not a customer approval.
stages.blocked: If the expected draft says “you have 10 days left”, return to the disagreement. If RE-7 does not settle the question, seek a policy decision rather than inventing one.

stages.title: Check the reviewed answer and assign the case to the right test group
stages.collaborator: Data steward and a reviewer who did not settle the earlier disagreement
stages.action: An independent reviewer compares resolution A12 with RE-7 and scoring rules R1. QA checks required fields, duplicates and the preserved original reviews. QA also runs the scoring check on an answer that should pass and one that should fail. The data steward records that the team has already seen G-12.
stages.before:
G-12.status = adjudicated
split = unassigned
scorer check = untested
stages.after:
G-12.status = validated
split = regression (already discussed and exposed)
label audit = referral-required agrees with RE-7/R1
original reviews = retained
positive control = expected draft passes
negative control = “Yes, you have 10 days left” fails
stages.artifact: Validation record V12 contains the independent label review, related-case checks, assigned test group and the passing/failing sample results.
stages.gate: All required checks must pass. Keep related cases in the same data group. Use G-12 as a regression case to catch repeat mistakes; reserve separately collected cases that the team has not used during improvement as the release holdout.
stages.blocked: If “Yes, you have 10 days left” passes, fix the scoring check before proceeding. If the source review disagrees, reopen the policy resolution. If the question lacks necessary facts, return to the candidate step.

stages.title: Save a fixed version of the reviewed reference set
stages.owner: Dataset owner, accountable for the reference set and its permitted use
stages.action: Save reference version pause-regression-v1 with G-12, RE-7 revision 1, scoring rules R1 and validation V12. Keep a read-only version record or a checksum that detects content changes. Store later model-test results separately from these expected answers.
stages.before:
Validated working copy
G-12.resolved = referral-required
split = regression
stages.after:
reference version = pause-regression-v1
G-12 source = RE-7 revision 1
G-12 resolved = referral-required
G-12 split = regression
reviews + A12 + V12 = retained
model result = not yet measured
stages.artifact: The version manifest is a contents record linking the cases, handbook and scoring-rule versions, test group and review records. Each later model run separately records its model version, prompt instructions and actual results.
stages.gate: After QA passes, the dataset owner accepts the reference’s intended use and limits. “Frozen” means this version stays unchanged for comparisons; it proves neither model quality nor permission to release.
stages.blocked: Do not change G-12 inside version v1 after using it in a run. If a label is wrong or the policy changes, open a new working version and keep v1 available for interpreting its old results.

stages.title: Reopen after policy or evidence changes
stages.collaborator: Policy owner, data steward and QA
stages.action: The policy owner publishes fictional RE-7 revision 2: up to two pauses per 12 months, combined maximum 30 days; an adviser must confirm eligibility. Copy G-12 into a new working version for independent review. Keep the old case and its old expected answer unchanged.
stages.before:
pause-regression-v1 remains frozen
RE-7 revision 1 = one pause per 12 months
G-12 resolved = referral-required
stages.after:
pause-regression-v2 draft
source = RE-7 revision 2: “Up to two pauses per 12 months; combined maximum 30 days; an adviser must confirm eligibility.”
question = unchanged
prior 1 pause + proposed 1 = 2; 20 + 10 = 30 days
proposed label = adviser-confirmation-required
resolved = unset pending independent review
old v1 resolution = preserved
stages.artifact: Change record C12 identifies the changed clause, affected case and new draft. The proposed label still needs review and does not approve a customer request.
stages.gate: First confirm that revision 2 is authorised and applies to this case. Repeat independent reviewer labels, resolve disagreements if needed, run QA checks and save a fixed new version. The new draft may say the numerical limits fit, but it must still require adviser confirmation.
stages.blocked: Never silently rescore historical runs using revision 2. If it is unclear which version applies, return to the first step. Keep revision 1’s results linked to revision 1.
